crit: Synthetic: 'the family of synthetic datasets used in prior research on the role of borderline examples [40]', with three minority-class shapes (sub-cluster, clover, paw), IR 5 and 7 and five disturbance ratios (0-70%) of borderline examples. Real-world: 'The choice of the real-world datasets was based on the work on imbalanced classification with noisy and borderline examples presented in [40]'; 'As the number of noisy examples is quite high compared to the size of the minority class these data sets are chosen to study their impact.' Noisy versions: real-world data 'transformed into more complex and even more difficult versions with an artificially increased noise level' (class and attribute noise, 20% and 40%).
benchmark_inherited_from: Napierala, Stefanowski & Wilk [40] (2010), 'Learning from imbalanced data in presence of noisy and borderline examples' (synthetic and real-world datasets)
notes: Three data types: 30 synthetic 2-D datasets (sub-cluster/clover/paw x IR 5 (600 examples) or IR 7 (800 examples) x DR 0/30/50/60/70%), 9 real-world datasets (Table 1, p.192), and noisy versions of the real-world sets (class or attribute noise at x=20% and 40%, Table 9). acl was 'provided by the authors of [45]' (not a public repository), coded Private; the other real-world sets are from KEEL. Binarisation sentence is in passive voice ('Multi-class datasets are modified ...'); coded binarised_by=authors because the paper describes the merge rule itself and names its own minority classes (Min column: e.g. imU, hyper, positive), but it could be inherited from [40]. Synthetic data generated by the software of [40]/[46] (co-author Stefanowski), not newly generated here. Synthetic dataset sizes and IRs are printed only in the text (p.190), not per dataset; minority counts for synthetic sets are not printed. modified_data_released=yes rests on the web page holding 'the datasets used' (noisy versions not explicitly mentioned). Extra classifiers (k-NN, SVM, RIPPER, PART) only on the web page.
